subject: [PATCH v7 0/6] fuse: add io-uring buffer pools and zero-copy

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a merge conflict in the io-uring patches, specifically in the io_uring/rsrc.c file where the code for registering request buffers was split into two versions. She provides a patch to resolve the conflict by reverting one of the changes and explains that this series is ready for the upcoming merge window.

2026-08-14.patch_summary: This patch series adds support for io-uring buffer pools and zero-copy to the FUSE file system, allowing servers to pass in a contiguous chunk of memory that the kernel can use to service requests. This reduces memory usage requirements and enables optimizations for assigning payload memory to requests. Additionally, it introduces zero-copy functionality, which allows direct access to client pages or page cache folios without copying data through an intermediary buffer, requiring CAP_SYS_ADMIN privileges and using buffer pools.

reviews.author: Miklos Szeredi
reviews.summary: Reviewer Miklos Szeredi reported a failure of the patch when tested with loraw, a loopback tester that doesn't use libfuse, resulting in an assertion error due to an invalid return code (-22) from io_uring. The reproducer is attached for further analysis.
reviews.raw_body:
I tested this with loraw (a "raw" loopback tester that doesn't use
libfuse) and it fails with

root@kvm:~# ./loraw -u  /mnt/fuse
loraw: loraw.c:1010: lo_start_uring: Assertion `!cqe->res' failed.

cqe->res is -22 (EINVAL).

Attaching the reproducer.  To compile:

cp $(KERNEL_TREE)/include/uapi/linux/fuse.h fuse_kernel.h
gcc loraw.c -oloraw -luring

Thanks,
Miklos

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: The author acknowledged a bug in the patch where it relies on an optional FUSE_OVER_IO_URING init reply to create the fuse ring, which can cause issues if not set by the server. They plan to fix this by creating the ring on the first io-uring command instead of at FUSE_INIT or FUSE_IO_URING_CMD_REGISTER ent creation time.

reviews.author: Bernd Schubert
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that io-uring should only be enabled when FUSE_OVER_IO_URING is set, and that this check was missing in the original patch. They also mentioned a potential lock order issue between queue->lock and fch->bg_lock, which needs to be addressed.

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledges that the patch will break backwards compatibility if changed and cites a specific kernel version as evidence.

The author addressed a concern that the fuse io-uring logic proceeds even if the server didn't reply with FUSE_OVER_IO_URING, explaining that this is due to an && condition in fuse_uring_cmd(). The author confirmed that enable_uring=1 is required for the kernel to advertise FUSE_OVER_IO_URING.
reviews.raw_body:
This is pre-existing behavior that's been there since the beginning
(kernel version 6.14) [1]. I don't think we can change this now, or
it'll break backwards compatibility, like Miklos's loraw program.

---

The condition check in fuse_uring_cmd() is an && and not an ||. It
doesn't enforce that the server must have sent over FUSE_OVER_IO_URING
in the init reply to use fuse io-uring. With enable_uring=1 (which is
needed for the kernel to advertise FUSE_OVER_IO_URING in the init
request in the first place), the fuse io-uring logic proceeds
regardless of whether the server replied with the FUSE_OVER_IO_URING
flag or not.

Thanks,
Joanne

[1] https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v6.14-rc1/source/fs/fuse/inode.c#L1455

reviews.author: Bernd Schubert
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that there is a lock order inversion issue in fuse_uring_queue_bq_req(), which would be resolved by distributing fch->num_background among queues, and also pointed out that the condition in fuse_block_alloc() doesn't make sense without FUSE_OVER_IO_URING reply.
sentiment_signals: condition in fuse_block_alloc() doesn't make sense
reviews.raw_body:
The comment there is definitely outdated, at least it was *supposed* to.

Well, then we have a problem because we have a lock order inversion
issue. After adding in the reduce-queue series I had planned to work on
distributing fch->num_background among queues, so that each queue gets
its own num_background, so that holding two locks like in
fuse_uring_queue_bq_req() wouldn't be needed anymore.

Also again, without FUSE_OVER_IO_URING reply the condition in
fuse_block_alloc() doesn't make any sense.


Thanks,
Bernd

reviews.author: Bernd Schubert
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted a lock order inversion issue in fuse_uring_cmd() where it takes queue->lock while holding fch->bg_lock, which can lead to a deadlock when legacy background completion paths are executed concurrently. They also pointed out an incorrect '&&' operator that allows userspace to bypass the module option for enabling io-uring.
reviews.raw_body:
Lock order inversion is this

 CPU 0 - io-uring completion              | CPU 1 - legacy background completion
                                           | fuse_request_end()
                                           |   takes fch->bg_lock
                                           |   fuse_request_bg_finish()
  fuse_uring_cmd()                         |
    fuse_uring_commit_fetch()              |
      fuse_uring_commit()                  |   
        fuse_uring_req_end()               |
          takes queue->lock                |
          wants fch->bg_lock               |
                                           |   flush_bg_queue()
                                           |     fuse_send_one()
                                           |       fiq->ops->send_req()
                                           |         fuse_uring_queue_fuse_req()
                                           |           wants queue->lock


(I queried AI about it to quickly generate that graph, but that is
exactly what I had seen back in development and which is why fuse
requests are supposed to be blocked until queue initialization is
complete, i.e. to avoid switching from /dev/fuse to io-uring at
run time.

The wrong "&&" in fuse_uring_cmd() also makes it possible that people
bypass the module option to enable io-uring, by just setting the flag
in their userspace implementation. Yikes :/
